answers.body: the Government makes every required payment and the investments earn about 5.8% a year. The actuary’s plan pays the 75% for as long as members live.
This plan only covers 75%. The other 25% was never part of it, and the Government stopped paying it after 2025.
The plan depends on the Government paying on time every year. Investments below 5.8% would also mean the Government has to pay more.

ghli.text: The Secretary of Finance warns that the Aetna contract ends December 31 and that $7.2M is needed to keep retirees covered.
The House passes HB 24-75 with $2.8M for retiree health and life insurance, leaving a $4.4M gap. The Settlement Fund urges retirees to look at other options.
The Governor signs the revised FY 2026 budget, Public Law 24-20, with $4.3M more for GHLI. The Aetna contract is renewed.
The Secretary of Finance estimates GHLI will cost the general fund about $11.9M in FY 2027, including $6.4M for retiree health.
The House passes the FY 2027 budget, HB 24-108, setting aside half of certain special accounts for retirees’ benefits, including GHLI. It now goes to the Senate.

risks.title: The Government pays late or less
risks.body: The whole plan assumes every required payment arrives. Missed or late payments are the single biggest threat to the 75%.

risks.title: Investments earn less than 5.8%
risks.body: Over the past five and ten years, returns were below the goal. If that continues, the actuary will ask the Government for more each year.

risks.title: Members live longer than expected
risks.body: Good news for families, but it means paying benefits for more years than planned.

risks.title: Health insurance depends on each year’s budget
risks.body: Coverage is not part of the Fund. If the Government’s budget falls short, retiree health insurance is at risk, as it nearly was in December 2025.

risks.title: After 2048, it all depends on the Government
risks.body: Once the account is empty, benefits must be paid from the Government’s budget each year.
